title: 2 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 18.

questions.question: In which year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel did Hezekiah begin to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Third year
questions.explanation: Hezekiah began to reign in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel as stated in 2 Kings 18:1.

questions.question: How old was Hezekiah when he began to reign as king of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-five
questions.explanation: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign according to 2 Kings 18:2.

questions.question: What was the name of Hezekiah's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Abi
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's mother's name was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah, as mentioned in 2 Kings 18:2.

questions.question: According to the chapter, Hezekiah did what was right in the sight of the LORD according to whom?
questions.correctAnswer: David his father
questions.explanation: Hezekiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father did, as stated in 2 Kings 18:3.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do to the brasen serpent that Moses had made?
options: He moved it to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: He broke it in pieces
questions.explanation: Hezekiah broke in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made, calling it Nehushtan, as described in 2 Kings 18:4.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Hezekiah's trust according to the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hezekiah trusted in the LORD God of Israel and none were like him among the kings of Judah, as stated in 2 Kings 18:5.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah rebelled against the king of Assyria and served him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hezekiah rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him, as stated in 2 Kings 18:7.

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah defeat, extending his control even to Gaza?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: Hezekiah smote the Philistines even unto Gaza and its borders, as recorded in 2 Kings 18:8.

questions.question: In which year of King Hezekiah did Shalmaneser king of Assyria come up against Samaria?
questions.correctAnswer: Fourth year
questions.explanation: Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against Samaria in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, as per 2 Kings 18:9.

questions.question: How long did the siege of Samaria last before it was taken?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: The siege lasted three years before Samaria was taken, according to 2 Kings 18:10.

questions.question: Where did the king of Assyria carry away Israel after taking Samaria?
questions.correctAnswer: Assyria
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria carried Israel away into Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and cities of the Medes as stated in 2 Kings 18:11.

questions.question: Why did the king of Assyria take Israel captive, according to the chapter?
options: Because they transgressed the LORD's covenant
Because they made alliances with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Because they transgressed the LORD's covenant
questions.explanation: Israel was taken because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD their God and transgressed his covenant, as in 2 Kings 18:12.

questions.question: True or False: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against the fenced cities of Judah and took them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Sennacherib came up against the fenced cities of Judah and took them in Hezekiah's fourteenth year, as stated in 2 Kings 18:13.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hezekiah reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, as recorded in 2 Kings 18:2.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 18, which event came first?
options: Sennacherib came against Judah's fenced cities
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah broke the brasen serpent
questions.explanation: Hezekiah broke the brasen serpent early in his reign (verse 4) before the siege of Samaria (verses 9-10) and before Sennacherib's attack (verse 13). He also smote the Philistines early but the breaking of the serpent is mentioned prior in the text.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah offer to the king of Assyria to stop his attack?
options: Three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold
All the silver found in the house of the LORD and treasures of the king's house
A treaty of peace and alliance
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:14 states Hezekiah sent to Assyria saying he had offended and was willing to bear what was put on him, and the king of Assyria appointed to him three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold. This was an offering to stop the attack.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah give to the king of Assyria as payment from the treasures of Jerusalem?
options: All the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the treasures of the king's house
Only the gold from the temple doors
questions.correctAnswer: All the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the treasures of the king's house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:15 specifically says Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the king's treasures to the Assyrian king as part of the payment.

questions.question: What action did Hezekiah take regarding the gold from the temple during the Assyrian threat?
options: He cut off the gold from the doors and pillars and gave it to the king of Assyria
He hid the gold to prevent it from being taken
He melted the gold down to make weapons
He refused to give any gold to the Assyrians
questions.correctAnswer: He cut off the gold from the doors and pillars and gave it to the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:16 records that Hezekiah removed the gold from the temple doors and pillars which he had overlaid and gave it to the king of Assyria, showing his willingness to pay tribute.

questions.question: Who did the king of Assyria send from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great host?
questions.correctAnswer: Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:17 states that the king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a great host against Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who came out to meet the Assyrian envoys when they called to the king of Judah?
options: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:18 describes that Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah came out to the Assyrian envoys when called upon, representing the king's officials.

questions.question: What was the main question Rabshakeh asked the envoys to speak to Hezekiah about?
options: What confidence or trust did Hezekiah have to rebel against Assyria?
Whether Hezekiah would surrender his city immediately
If Hezekiah was willing to pay more tribute
If Hezekiah wished to form an alliance with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: What confidence or trust did Hezekiah have to rebel against Assyria?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:19 shows Rabshakeh asking the envoys to tell Hezekiah, 'What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?' questioning Hezekiah's rebellion against Assyria.

questions.question: According to Rabshakeh, on whom did Hezekiah put his trust that was likened to a bruised reed?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh king of Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:21 states that Hezekiah trusted on 'the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt,' implying Pharaoh king of Egypt is an unreliable support.

questions.question: What did Rabshakeh say about trusting in the LORD God in light of Hezekiah's reforms?
options: He questioned it because Hezekiah had removed high places and altars, commanding worship only in Jerusalem
He fully acknowledged the LORD's power
He encouraged the people to trust the LORD instead of Hezekiah
He claimed the LORD had sent Assyria to destroy Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned it because Hezekiah had removed high places and altars, commanding worship only in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:22 records Rabshakeh challenging the trust in the LORD by pointing out that Hezekiah had taken away high places and altars, insisting worship in Jerusalem alone.

questions.question: What did Rabshakeh offer as a pledge to deliver to Hezekiah if he could set riders upon them?
questions.correctAnswer: Two thousand horses
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 18:23, Rabshakeh offers to deliver two thousand horses if Hezekiah could set riders upon them, mocking Judah's military capability.

questions.question: What reason did Rabshakeh give for coming up against Jerusalem, according to his own words?
options: The LORD had commanded him to destroy the land
Hezekiah had refused to pay tribute
He sought to expand the Assyrian empire
The people of Judah rebelled violently
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD had commanded him to destroy the land
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:25 states Rabshakeh claimed he came up not without the LORD, but because the LORD said to him to go up and destroy the land, implying divine sanction for his invasion.

questions.question: Why did Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah request Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language instead of the Jews' language?
options: So the people on the wall would not understand the Assyrian threats
Because they did not understand the Jews' language
questions.correctAnswer: So the people on the wall would not understand the Assyrian threats
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:26 reveals their request for Rabshakeh to speak in Syrian so the Jewish people on the wall wouldn't understand the Assyrian threats and be discouraged.

questions.question: How did Rabshakeh respond to the request to speak in the Syrian language?
options: He refused and spoke in the Jews' language loudly so all could hear
He agreed and spoke quietly in Syrian
He sent a written message instead
questions.correctAnswer: He refused and spoke in the Jews' language loudly so all could hear
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:27-28 shows Rabshakeh refusing to speak in Syrian and instead loudly spoke in the Jews' language so all the people could hear his message.

questions.question: According to Rabshakeh, what will happen if the people listen to Hezekiah's claim that the LORD will deliver them?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:30-32 records Rabshakeh's warning not to trust Hezekiah's words that the LORD will deliver them, as Rabshakeh asserts the city will be delivered into Assyria's hand.

questions.question: Did the people respond to Rabshakeh's speech, and what was the king's command about responding?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:36 states the people held their peace and answered him not a word because the king commanded them not to respond to Rabshakeh's words.

questions.question: What did Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah do after Rabshakeh's speech to the people?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:37 reports that after the speech, these officials came to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, indicating mourning and distress, to report Rabshakeh's words.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 18.

questions.question: What was Rabshakeh’s purpose in speaking to the men on the wall in the Jews' language instead of the Syrian language?
options: To intimidate the people and cause fear
To ensure the people on the wall could understand his threats directly
To secretly communicate with the leaders
To mock the people in a language they did not understand
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure the people on the wall could understand his threats directly
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh deliberately spoke in the Jews' language so that the people on the wall would hear his words and be demoralized, as stated in 2 Kings 18:28 where he stood and cried in the Jews' language.

questions.question: According to Rabshakeh, why should the people not trust in Egypt for help against Assyria?
options: Because Egypt was too far to reach
Because Egypt was like a bruised reed that will pierce the hand
Because Egypt was an ally of Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Because Egypt was like a bruised reed that will pierce the hand
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh compared Egypt to a bruised reed that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it, illustrating its unreliability, as described in 2 Kings 18:21.

questions.question: What was one major reason given for the exile of Israel by the king of Assyria?
options: They disobeyed the LORD and transgressed His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They disobeyed the LORD and transgressed His covenant
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria carried Israel away because they did not obey the voice of the LORD, transgressed His covenant, and ignored Moses’ commandments, as explained in 2 Kings 18:12.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do with the gold from the doors and pillars of the temple of the LORD?
options: Used it to fund temple repairs
Gave it as a present to the king of Assyria
Melted it down to make new idols
Kept it hidden in the treasury
questions.correctAnswer: Gave it as a present to the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Hezekiah cut off the gold from the temple doors and pillars and gave it to the king of Assyria as a tribute, according to 2 Kings 18:16.

questions.question: Who were the officials that came out to meet Rabshakeh when he called to the king?
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah
questions.explanation: Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebna the scribe, and Joah the recorder came out to meet Rabshakeh as stated in 2 Kings 18:18.

questions.question: What was the king of Assyria’s claim regarding the gods of other nations compared to the LORD of Israel?
options: The gods of other nations had helped them defeat Assyria
No gods of the nations had delivered their lands from Assyria’s hand
The gods of Israel were stronger than Assyria’s gods
The gods of other nations were false gods
questions.correctAnswer: No gods of the nations had delivered their lands from Assyria’s hand
questions.explanation: The king challenged the people by asking where the gods of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah were, stating none had delivered their lands from Assyria, as seen in 2 Kings 18:34.

questions.question: How did the people respond to Rabshakeh’s speech on the wall?
options: They fell to their knees and prayed
They held their peace and answered not a word
questions.correctAnswer: They held their peace and answered not a word
questions.explanation: The people remained silent as commanded by their king, not answering Rabshakeh’s provocations, as stated in 2 Kings 18:36.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Rabshakeh’s speech when he compares Egypt to a bruised reed?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh uses a simile by saying Egypt is like a bruised reed that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it, comparing Egypt’s unreliability using 'like', found in 2 Kings 18:21.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word translated as 'bruised reed' in 2 Kings 18:21 conveys a fragile but dangerous object?
questions.correctAnswer: Qashash
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'qashash' can mean a broken or bruised reed, symbolizing fragility that can cause harm, fitting the metaphor in 2 Kings 18:21.

questions.question: The sending of Rabshakeh and his officers to Jerusalem with a great host reflects what historical Near Eastern military tactic?
options: Siege warfare combined with psychological warfare
questions.correctAnswer: Siege warfare combined with psychological warfare
questions.explanation: Sending a large army and a spokesman to taunt and demoralize the city’s defenders was a common Assyrian tactic to weaken resistance before siege, as seen in 2 Kings 18:17.

questions.question: How does the challenge by the king of Assyria in 2 Kings 18:33-35 reflect a theological challenge to the faith in the LORD?
options: It denies the existence of the LORD
It questions the LORD’s ability to save like other gods
It acknowledges the LORD’s power over other gods
It demands the people worship other gods
questions.correctAnswer: It questions the LORD’s ability to save like other gods
questions.explanation: The king mocks the idea that the LORD would deliver Jerusalem by comparing Him to powerless gods who failed to save their nations, directly challenging Israel’s faith, as in 2 Kings 18:35.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of trusting in God rather than worldly powers as seen in 2 Kings 18:30?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 20:7
questions.explanation: Psalm 20:7 contrasts trust in chariots and horses with trust in the name of the LORD, echoing the theme of reliance on God over military or political alliances found in 2 Kings 18:30.

questions.question: How does Hezekiah’s act of removing the brasen serpent (Nehushtan) in 2 Kings 18:4 foreshadow New Testament teachings?
options: It foreshadows the destruction of idols by Paul
It prefigures the lifting up of Christ for salvation
It predicts the building of the temple in the New Testament
It indicates the rejection of Moses’ law
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the lifting up of Christ for salvation
questions.explanation: The brasen serpent was lifted up to bring healing, prefiguring Christ’s crucifixion lifted up for salvation, as referenced in John 3:14-15, connecting to 2 Kings 18:4.

questions.question: What was the authorial intent behind recording Rabshakeh’s blasphemous speech in the Jews' language in this chapter?
options: To show the Assyrian king’s respect for Israel
To highlight the psychological warfare and test of faith faced by Judah
To confuse the readers about historical events
questions.correctAnswer: To highlight the psychological warfare and test of faith faced by Judah
questions.explanation: The speech demonstrates the intense pressure and challenge to Judah’s faith, emphasizing the spiritual and psychological conflict described in 2 Kings 18:28-30.

questions.question: What cross-biblical connection can be drawn between Hezekiah’s reliance on God in this chapter and the New Testament example of Jesus’ reliance on the Father?
options: Both show trust in God despite worldly threats
questions.correctAnswer: Both show trust in God despite worldly threats
questions.explanation: Hezekiah trusts God when threatened by Assyria, paralleling Jesus’ dependence on God during His temptation and ministry, highlighting faith under trial (2 Kings 18:5; Matthew 4:1-11).

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific act of religious reform did Hezekiah perform that reflects the doctrine of sanctification and the rejection of idolatry?
options: He removed the high places and broke the brazen serpent called Nehushtan
He built new altars to foreign gods
He encouraged incense burning to Moses' serpent
He allowed worship in multiple locations
questions.correctAnswer: He removed the high places and broke the brazen serpent called Nehushtan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:4 explains that Hezekiah removed high places, broke images, cut down groves, and broke the brazen serpent called Nehushtan because the people burned incense to it, demonstrating sanctification by purging idolatry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD's presence and blessing on Hezekiah's endeavors according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:7 states that the LORD was with Hezekiah and he prospered wherever he went, showing God's providential care and guidance over His chosen king’s actions.

questions.question: How does the exile of Israel by the king of Assyria illustrate the doctrine of divine judgment for covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Because Israel did not obey the LORD and transgressed His covenant, they were carried into exile
Because Israel trusted the LORD, they were protected from exile
Because Israel made treaties with other nations, they were exiled
Because Israel built high places, they were rewarded
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel did not obey the LORD and transgressed His covenant, they were carried into exile
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:11-12 explain that Israel was taken into Assyrian captivity because they disobeyed the LORD and broke His covenant, reflecting divine judgment on covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Hezekiah’s trust in the LORD alone rather than in Egypt as depicted in this chapter?
options: It reveals the doctrine of divine sovereignty over nations and the futility of trusting in human power
It shows that Hezekiah was politically naive
It emphasizes military strategy over faith
It indicates that Egypt was a faithful ally
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the doctrine of divine sovereignty over nations and the futility of trusting in human power
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:21 shows Rabshakeh mocking trust in Egypt as a bruised reed that will pierce the hand of those who lean on it, illustrating that trusting in human powers is futile compared to trusting God.

questions.question: How does the king of Assyria's speech in this chapter serve as an apologetic challenge to faith in God's deliverance?
options: He claims that no god of nations has delivered their land from Assyria's hand, challenging belief in divine protection
He admits the LORD will deliver Jerusalem
He praises Hezekiah's faith in the LORD
He offers peace to Judah based on their faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: He claims that no god of nations has delivered their land from Assyria's hand, challenging belief in divine protection
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:33-35 records the Assyrian king’s rhetorical questions doubting any gods delivering nations from Assyria, directly challenging the faith in God's power to save, making it an apologetic objection addressed in Scripture.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Hezekiah’s action of giving all the silver and gold from the temple and king’s treasures to Assyria?
options: Submission to worldly powers under divine sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Submission to worldly powers under divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:15-16 show Hezekiah paying tribute to Assyria by giving silver and gold, illustrating submission to earthly authorities as allowed within divine sovereignty (cf. Romans 13:1).

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Kings 18:5-6 and 2 Kings 18:11 convey about the relationship between trusting God and covenant obedience?
options: Trust in God is linked to covenant faithfulness, while disobedience leads to exile
Trust in God is unrelated to covenant obedience
Obedience guarantees earthly prosperity without exception
Covenant obedience is irrelevant to Israel’s fate
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God is linked to covenant faithfulness, while disobedience leads to exile
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:5-6 describes Hezekiah’s trust and obedience to God, and 18:11 shows Israel’s exile due to disobedience, together teaching that trusting God is inseparable from covenant obedience, with disobedience resulting in judgment.

questions.question: How does Hezekiah’s reign as described in 2 Kings 18:1-3 fit into the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: Hezekiah’s righteous reign continues the Davidic covenant promise of a godly king
Hezekiah reigns as an idolatrous king
Hezekiah’s reign is insignificant to redemptive history
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah’s righteous reign continues the Davidic covenant promise of a godly king
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:1-3 notes Hezekiah did right as David did, fitting him as a faithful Davidic king in the covenantal promise of a godly ruler in Judah's redemptive history (cf. 2 Samuel 7).

questions.question: What is the doctrinal significance of the king of Assyria being described as acting with the LORD’s permission in 2 Kings 18:25?
options: It shows God's sovereign control over even hostile nations to accomplish His purposes
It suggests the king of Assyria is a true believer
It implies the LORD supports idolatry
It denies God's involvement in human history
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's sovereign control over even hostile nations to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:25 says the LORD told the Assyrian king to go up and destroy the land, demonstrating divine sovereignty over nations, using even enemies to fulfill His judgment and plans.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s holiness and exclusivity is highlighted by Rabshakeh’s taunt about Hezekiah removing high places and altars in 2 Kings 18:22?
options: God’s demand for exclusive worship and rejection of idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: God’s demand for exclusive worship and rejection of idolatry
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh in 2 Kings 18:22 mocks Hezekiah for removing altars and high places, indirectly affirming that the LORD demands exclusive worship at the designated place, highlighting God’s holiness and intolerance of idolatry.

questions.question: What synthesis of verses 2 Kings 18:13 and 2 Kings 18:37 teaches about the human response to divine crisis and leadership communication?
options: In crisis, leaders must receive reports with humility and seek God’s guidance
Leaders should ignore threats and avoid communication
Silence is the best response to enemies
Leaders must respond with military might alone
questions.correctAnswer: In crisis, leaders must receive reports with humility and seek God’s guidance
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:13 records Assyria’s conquest of Judean cities, and 18:37 shows officials reporting Rabshakeh’s words to Hezekiah with torn clothes, a sign of mourning and humility, teaching leaders to humbly receive warnings and seek God’s help in trials.

questions.question: What attribute of God is especially evident in 2 Kings 18:6 concerning Hezekiah’s faithfulness to God's commandments?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness in commanding obedience
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:6 emphasizes that Hezekiah kept the commandments the LORD gave through Moses, highlighting God’s holy nature that demands obedience and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the Assyrian king’s offer of horses and riders in 2 Kings 18:23 reflect his view of power contrasted with the biblical view of divine sovereignty?
options: He relies on military might, ignoring God’s sovereign power
He offers peace based on faith in God
He shows humility before Judah’s God
questions.correctAnswer: He relies on military might, ignoring God’s sovereign power
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:23 shows the Assyrian king boasting about his military resources, ignoring the biblical teaching that true power and deliverance come from God’s sovereign hand.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do 2 Kings 18:14 and 2 Kings 18:15-16 provide about the tension between political expediency and spiritual fidelity?
options: Hezekiah’s payment to Assyria reveals compromise under pressure but risks spiritual defilement
Hezekiah’s actions show full trust in God without compromise
The chapter teaches that political alliances always honor God
Hezekiah’s tribute had no spiritual consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah’s payment to Assyria reveals compromise under pressure but risks spiritual defilement
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:14-16 describe Hezekiah’s tribute payment to Assyria including temple gold, reflecting political compromise that jeopardizes spiritual purity, highlighting tension between survival and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the narrative of 2 Kings 18:9-10 about Samaria’s siege and fall fit the broader redemptive theme of judgment and restoration in Scripture?
options: It shows judgment for covenant unfaithfulness, setting the stage for future restoration
It shows permanent abandonment of Israel without hope
It suggests God’s rejection of the Davidic covenant
It denies any consequences for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It shows judgment for covenant unfaithfulness, setting the stage for future restoration
questions.explanation: The siege and capture of Samaria in 2 Kings 18:9-10 illustrate God’s judgment on Israel’s covenant breach, a theme that, while severe, anticipates future restoration (cf. Isaiah 11).
